hanbi_route.092: It sounds smaller out loud than it did in the archive. Sixteen and already tired of packing.
hanbi_route.094: "I don't know yet. I've never stayed anywhere long enough to find out."
hanbi_route.095: …That's okay. You don't have to know yet.
hanbi_route.097: …I will. I'll set an alarm. Songha will be so proud.
hanbi_route.098: "I'm sitting on the worst sofa in Seoul, and I don't want to get up."
hanbi_route.099: He looks down at the sofa. Then at you. The tips of his ears go pink again, in real colour this time.
hanbi_route.101: I wrote my letter the same week. I think.
hanbi_route.104: I thought, if I drew it well enough, I wouldn't have to write anything.
hanbi_route.105: The lamp flickers. Somewhere above you, ECHO is running out of building.
hanbi_route.106: Hanbi looks at the old portrait. Then at you. Then he says — out loud, to the ceiling, in the voice of someone who isn't used to asking for anything:
hanbi_route.107: ECHO. …Can you open it one more time?
hanbi_route.108: Not for me. For both of us. I want to try something.
hanbi_route.109: Request received from the owner of RECORD 01.
hanbi_route.110: It is 04:12. I have time for one more reconstruction.
hanbi_route.111: …I would like to spend it on this.
hanbi_route.112: The lounge folds itself back into paper.
hanbi_route.113: The dust sheets go first, lifting and thinning into white. The sofa becomes the outline of a sofa. The window fills with slanting pencil rain.
hanbi_route.114: But this time the room is empty. No sleeping musician. No kids with noodles. No figure of light at the desk.
hanbi_route.115: Just the two of you, and a room that hasn't been drawn yet.
hanbi_route.117: The Future Letter desk. The broken sharpener, still clamped to the corner. You sit, and the chair takes your weight as if it's been expecting you.
hanbi_route.118: Hanbi takes the armchair in the corner. He's too tall for it now. He sits in it anyway, sketchbook on his knee, the way he did at sixteen.
hanbi_route.119: …I'm going to draw. And while I draw, I'm going to say things. Out loud.
hanbi_route.121: It'll be bad. Just so you know.
hanbi_route.124: "Do I have to hold still for this?"
hanbi_route.126: Fold your hands on the desk and hold still.
hanbi_route.127: He watches you settle. Something in his shoulders settles too.
hanbi_route.128: The pencil moves. Wherever it touches his page, a line of light rises from the floor and draws itself into the room.
hanbi_route.129: The edge of the desk, firmer. The lamp.
hanbi_route.130: …In the alley. When you came out of the rain.
hanbi_route.131: I wanted to give you my coat. I gave you a nod instead.
hanbi_route.132: It was a very small nod.
hanbi_route.133: The lamp on the desk warms to amber, as if someone breathed on it.
hanbi_route.134: At the door. When you went in first.
hanbi_route.135: I wanted to say that was brave. Nobody else moved. I didn't move.
hanbi_route.136: At the door. When you made Daniel go first.
hanbi_route.137: I wanted to say thank you. He was scared. He needed a job.
hanbi_route.138: At the door. When I went in first, I looked back to see if you were okay.
hanbi_route.139: I wanted to say I'd wait. If you weren't.
hanbi_route.140: The window turns blue-grey. Real rain, behind drawn glass.
hanbi_route.141: The water. It was mine. I wanted to say— I'd rather you had it.
hanbi_route.142: The floorboards warm to honey, board by board, from his chair to yours.
hanbi_route.143: And in the room. When you coloured it.
hanbi_route.144: I wanted to say it's the only page in that sketchbook I didn't do alone.
hanbi_route.145: Beneath nobody at all, the sofa floods with its terrible orange. He almost laughs. He keeps drawing.
hanbi_route.146: Then the pencil stops. It hovers over the page, over the place where your face would go.
hanbi_route.149: It's just— I think you probably already—
hanbi_route.152: He looks up. That's the only answer for a moment: he looks up, and doesn't look away.
hanbi_route.154: It would be so easy to finish the sentence for him. Everyone always does. You don't.
hanbi_route.155: Leave the desk. Go and sit on the arm of his chair.
hanbi_route.156: The armchair creaks. He looks up at you, so close that the sketchbook is the only thing between you, and he doesn't hide behind it.
hanbi_route.158: …That's the whole sentence. There's no dash at the end.
hanbi_route.159: I liked you in the alley. At the door. When you coloured the rain, or didn't. I liked you the whole time I wasn't saying it.
hanbi_route.160: I'd like to keep liking you. After five. Out loud.
hanbi_route.161: I want to see you again.
hanbi_route.162: …After five. After tonight. That's the whole sentence. There's no dash at the end.
hanbi_route.163: I don't know what it is yet. I'd like to find out slowly. With you actually there.
hanbi_route.164: The room doesn't fill, this time. It pours.
hanbi_route.165: Colour runs down the walls like rain running the right way for once. The desk, the curtains, the terrible sofa, the ceiling, the air.
hanbi_route.166: And everywhere his pencil has touched the page, laundromat yellow. The light that's always on.
hanbi_route.167: And everywhere his pencil has touched the page, exit-sign green. The light that's been doing its job all night.
hanbi_route.168: And everywhere his pencil has touched the page, vending-machine red. Small, and the first thing you see.
hanbi_route.169: And everywhere his pencil has touched the page, Archive Wall blue. The glow everyone looks at first.
hanbi_route.170: In the middle of it, a boy who isn't a boy any more sits in a chair too small for him.
hanbi_route.171: He's looking at you. He has, it seems, decided to stop apologising for it.
hanbi_route.172: "I'm not going anywhere. Not this time."
hanbi_route.176: "That was a lot more than five words."
hanbi_route.180: He holds out his hand — the left, the drawing hand, grey along the edge with graphite — and you take it.
hanbi_route.181: When you let go, a little of the grey has come off on your palm.
hanbi_route.185: Can I—? Just for a second.
hanbi_route.186: You nod. He leans in and rests his forehead against yours, very lightly, the way you'd check if paint is dry.
hanbi_route.187: A second. Then two. The drawn rain keeps falling. Neither of you counts.
hanbi_route.188: He holds out the pencil — his pencil, the one from behind his ear — and you both hold it for a moment, your fingers overlapping on the painted wood.
hanbi_route.191: …Keep them. I mean— give them back slowly.
hanbi_route.192: He turns back to the portrait. The oval where your face should be.
hanbi_route.193: He draws one line. Just one — soft, uncertain, somewhere near where a mouth might go.
hanbi_route.194: Then he stops, and looks at it, and puts the pencil back behind his ear.
hanbi_route.196: …I don't want to finish it in one sitting.
hanbi_route.197: The lounge comes back, dust sheets and all. The lamp. The orange sofa, which is somehow even worse after seeing it in full colour.
hanbi_route.198: You're sitting on it. You don't remember sitting down. His shoulder is next to yours, not touching, close enough to.
hanbi_route.199: Outside the round window in the door, a shadow pauses. A paper bag appears on the floor. The shadow leaves without knocking.
hanbi_route.200: Inside the bag: two triangle kimbap, two bottles of water, and a note in careful handwriting. *For hyung. And {{playerName}}. Please eat. — H.*
hanbi_route.203: …Both. Probably. They'll argue about who gets credit.
hanbi_route.204: He hands you one kimbap and one water before taking his own. Of course he does.
hanbi_route.205: He peels his kimbap one-handed. His other hand is still in yours, and he seems to have decided that's just how he eats now.
hanbi_route.206: He eats in small, careful bites, and every so often he looks over at you, just to check you're still there. You are.
hanbi_route.209: Nothing. I just wanted to say it out loud. While I can.
hanbi_route.210: All recipients to the lobby, please.
hanbi_route.211: It is 04:57. There is one thing left to choose.
hanbi_route.212: Hanbi folds the old portrait along its soft crease and puts it in his coat, next to the sketchbook.
hanbi_route.213: Then he stands and holds out his hand to help you up. Not to lead. Just in case you want it.
hanbi_ending.001: The Archive Wall has gone dark, box by box, until only one is left glowing. Box 01.
hanbi_ending.002: RECORD 01 — OWNER: HANBI. SELECTED FOR PRESERVATION.
hanbi_ending.003: Writing to glass. Please do not look directly at the glass. I am told that is a joke. Please look if you want to.
hanbi_ending.004: Light drains out of the wall and into a small rectangle of glass on the front desk. Line by line, the portrait draws itself inside it.
hanbi_ending.005: The lounge. The rain. The orange sofa, the only colour. A figure at a desk, writing, with no face.
hanbi_ending.006: Wait. It doesn't have a face. ECHO, it's broken. Somebody hit it.
hanbi_ending.007: It's not broken. It's Hanbi. He's been not-finishing things since I met him.
hanbi_ending.008: It's *so* pretty though. Can I hold it? Can I just— okay, no, I won't hold it. I'll look at it. Near it.
hanbi_ending.009: Wait, what's happening? Is that {{playerName}}? Is that the *orange sofa*?
hanbi_ending.010: It's the sofa. Nobody ever sat on it.
hanbi_ending.011: It's a good choice. The record. I think I would've chosen it too, honestly.
hanbi_ending.012: Justin, in the background, does a small, formal bow in Hanbi's direction, like a conductor at the end of a concert.
hanbi_ending.013: First record. First pick. Legendary, hyung.
hanbi_ending.015: He says "please stop" but he's not stopping us.
hanbi_ending.016: Hanbi picks up the glass card. It glows a little in his hands, the orange sofa bright as a coal.
hanbi_ending.017: He looks at it for a long time. Then he holds it out to you.
hanbi_ending.020: You're in it. You were always—
hanbi_ending.021: He stops. You watch him hear himself stop. He starts again.
hanbi_ending.022: You're in it. So it's yours. I'll keep the paper.
hanbi_ending.023: The others go quiet in the particular way of people pretending very hard not to watch.
hanbi_ending.024: …He finished a sentence. Did everyone see that? He restarted it and finished it.
hanbi_ending.027: The power is off. The lounge is lit the only way it can be now: grey-blue at first, then peach, climbing the dust sheets from the round window.
hanbi_ending.028: Upstairs, Songha is running what he calls an orderly exit and everyone else calls shouting. Somewhere, Daniel is saying goodbye to the claw machine.
hanbi_ending.029: Hanbi is on the orange sofa. You are on the orange sofa. Neither of you has suggested leaving it yet.
hanbi_ending.030: He takes the sketchbook out of his coat and opens it to the page from the drawn room. Then he turns it round, so you can see.
hanbi_ending.031: It's you, at the Future Letter desk. The borrowed pencil in your hand. The window, the rain, the lamp, all finished — careful and complete.
hanbi_ending.032: One colour on the whole page: laundromat yellow, in the light behind you.
hanbi_ending.033: One colour on the whole page: exit-sign green, in the light behind you.
hanbi_ending.034: One colour on the whole page: vending-machine red, in the light behind you.
hanbi_ending.035: One colour on the whole page: Archive Wall blue, in the light behind you.
hanbi_ending.036: And the face. One soft line where a mouth might go. The rest is still paper.
hanbi_ending.037: There's still a faint grey smudge on your palm, from the drawn room. You haven't wiped it off. You find you don't want to.
hanbi_ending.039: I hadn't decided how to draw you.
hanbi_ending.044: You have lived in four cities. You have left every one of them in spring.
hanbi_ending.045: You have never once sat still long enough for anybody to finish.
hanbi_ending.046: The sun comes up over the laundromat. The sofa is still the worst orange in Seoul.
hanbi_ending.051: Hanbi! Has anyone seen Hanbi? I need a charger! Hanbi!
hanbi_ending.052: His voice comes down the corridor, rising and falling. Somewhere above, a door opens and Charlie asks what's happening.
hanbi_ending.053: Hanbi doesn't move. He looks at the door. Then he looks back at you, and picks up his pencil.
hanbi_ending.055: He says it loud enough to carry. For once in his life, he lets somebody else wait.
hanbi_newmem.001: A week later. A café near the practice studio, ten in the morning, on a day so sunny it feels like a mistake.
hanbi_newmem.002: The message came last night, in three parts.
hanbi_newmem.003: are you free tomorrow. 10. I need a sitting
hanbi_newmem.005: bring nothing. I have extra pencils
hanbi_newmem.006: He has, in fact, brought extra pencils. Also two phone chargers, two umbrellas, a packet of tissues, and a small wrapped pastry he pushes across the table before saying hello.
hanbi_newmem.009: There isn't a cloud in the sky.
hanbi_newmem.011: He opens the sketchbook to a page headed, in small careful letters, *SITTING 2*. So far it contains three drawings of your hands and one of the pastry.
hanbi_newmem.012: Hold still. …You can eat. Just eat slowly.
hanbi_newmem.013: His phone buzzes. Then buzzes again. Then keeps buzzing, face down on the table, like it's trying to crawl away.
hanbi_newmem.014: Do you need to get that?
hanbi_newmem.015: He turns it over just long enough for you both to see the screen.
hanbi_newmem.019: ARE YOU GUYS GETTING FOOD WITHOUT US
hanbi_newmem.020: He turns it face down again. Gently. Like putting a small, noisy animal to bed.
hanbi_newmem.021: …Hyunjun will be here in twenty minutes. I'm sorry.
hanbi_newmem.023: …He always says "without us." Then he comes.
hanbi_newmem.024: For a while he just draws. The café hums around you. Your drink goes a little cold, and you let it.
hanbi_newmem.027: I know you know. I wanted to say it out loud anyway.
hanbi_newmem.029: Twenty minutes later, exactly, the café door bangs open, and the sun comes in with Hyunjun attached.
hanbi_newmem.030: Hanbi slides the second umbrella across the table to you without looking up. The sky is still perfectly clear.
